questions.solution:
For an ellipse $\frac{x^2}{A}+\frac{y^2}{B}=1$ with $A,B>0$, the major axis is along the y-axis when $B>A$.
Both denominators are positive because $f$ is positive, so the curve is always an ellipse.
The condition is therefore $f(3a+15) > f(a^2+7a+3)$.
$f$ is strictly decreasing, so $f(u)>f(v) \iff u<v$. This gives $3a+15 < a^2+7a+3$.
Rearrange: $a^2+4a-12>0$.
Factorise: $(a+6)(a-2)>0$.
So $a<-6$ or $a>2$, which means $a\in\mathbb{R}-[-6,2]$.
Hence $\alpha=-6$ and $\beta=2$.
Then $\alpha^2+\beta^2=36+4=40$.
Answer: (B) 40
